```flow
Connect the two teams once
Share one chat, project or note folder
They accept
Stop any time
```

You are running a piece of work with a client, an agency or a contractor. They need to see the tasks and talk to your people. They do not need to see everything else.

## Why it is hard

The usual choices are all awkward. Invite them into your workspace as members and you worry about what else they can reach. Keep them outside and the work runs over email: files attached and re-attached, status copied by hand, and two versions of the truth.

## How Genos helps

You share a single item with their team: one group chat, one project, or one restricted folder of team notes. First the two teams connect, once. The connection alone gives nobody access to anything. After that, each share is a separate decision that an owner or editor makes, and an owner or editor on the other side accepts.

On a shared project their people join as guests: they work in its tasks, comments, files, task notes and project chat, and cannot manage its members. Share a project or a chat only with people you are happy to have take part, not only watch. For a note folder you can choose **View only**, which lets them read without editing.

## What you get

- **One place for the shared work.** It appears in their workspace in the usual spot, and nobody needs a second account.
- **A clear boundary.** They see what you shared: not your other projects, chats or folders, and never your team's member list. Search and Genos AI follow the same boundary.
- **Less admin.** Their owner or editor adds and removes their own colleagues on that item. You can still remove any one of them.
- **A clean ending.** Stop sharing and everyone from that team loses access to the item at once. What they wrote stays with your team. Either side can do this.

## Good to know

A one-to-one direct message and a project chat cannot be shared on their own; a project share brings its chat with it. A team you share with cannot pass the item on to a third team. Each person's AI use counts against their own plan.

## How to start

1. Ask the other company for their **Team ID** (it is in their Team Profile).
2. In your Team Profile, open **Connected teams**, paste it and choose **Request connection**.
3. Once they approve, share the project from its profile with **Teams with access → Share with a connected team**.

Only an owner or editor of a team can connect or share, so ask yours if you do not see these options.
